title: Vocabulary Building
notes: A useful vocabulary note has the word, its word class, a short definition, and one sentence of your own. Three different sentences fix a meaning better than a synonym list alone.

A root carries the core meaning, as port means carry. A prefix changes that meaning, as in transport and export. A suffix often changes the word class, as in create, creation, and creative. Check a dictionary after the first guess.

Collocations are words that habitually go together: make a decision, do homework, strong tea, heavy rain. A sentence can be grammatical and still sound wrong if the pairing is off, as in do a decision.
In a passage, a definition may follow that is or a dash. An example after such as narrows the meaning. A contrast after but or unlike tells you what the word is not.

Register is how formal a word is. Kids and children, buy and purchase, ask and request can share a meaning and differ in tone. Match the word to the reader: a letter to a principal is more formal than a note to a friend.
